summary.intent: Implement Workstream 3 (PR #638) on the add/init interactive wizard: a rows-only selection mode in the tty picker when names can't be typed exactly, plus HashSet-based duplicate checks in the changeset writer and --package ingestion, with failing-first tests and the full gate, codex review loop, and a signed local commit.
summary.outcome: Failing-first tests were written and shown failing pre-fix, then the rows-only mode and linear duplicate checks were implemented. Full gate passed (pre-push, lint, doc-check, test all exit 0), spec and changeset were updated, and the commit was attempted unsandboxed after the sandbox blocked writing to .git/worktrees. The codex review rounds, final sha and report were not reached in this transcript.

repo: Picker selection lives in crates/callisto-cli/src/tty.rs and is shared by add and init, so the rows-only mode fixes both commands at one boundary.

Duplicate checks exist in two places that must stay consistent: the changeset writer in callisto-model (format/changeset/mod.rs) and --package ingestion in callisto-cli commands/add.rs; both are keyed by resolved owner, so aliases of one package still count as duplicates.
The picker listing is sorted, so row numbers in tests must follow sorted order (e.g. `a`, `a,b`, `b` makes `a,b` row 2).
The wizard is unreleased, so its existing changeset (.changeset/sharp-badgers-hunt.md) was extended instead of adding a new one.
CLI spec criteria for add and init live in docs/specs/cli.json and needed updating for the rows-only behaviour.
The gate (just pre-push, lint, doc-check, test) is workspace-wide and PTY/network tests must run unsandboxed.

code.finding: Writer duplicate check was a quadratic scan (67.6/261.0/1000.7 ms for N/2N/4N); replacing it with a HashSet gave 0.9/1.8/3.6 ms, linear.
Pre-fix, input such as `trail ` was accepted as `[0]` and short `trail` matched; names that can't round-trip the tokenizer now trigger a rows-only mode that refuses typed text with a re-ask.

workflow: Writing failing-first tests and capturing pre-fix failure output gives concrete oracle evidence; control tests that pass pre-fix demonstrate preservation.
Growth tests measured N/2N/4N ratios (about x2 per doubling when linear, about x4 when quadratic) instead of a CI time threshold.
Run a growth probe before and after the fix, then remove the probe so it is not committed.
Git commits in the worktree need an unsandboxed run because the sandbox blocks writes to .git/worktrees.
Writing the commit message to a file and committing with it avoided inline quoting problems.

friction: Sandbox blocked git commit writes to .git/worktrees, requiring an unsandboxed retry and a message file.
An initial test control expectation was wrong (display name is `dual`) and needed fixing.
The comma PTY test picked the wrong row because of sorted listing order and had to be corrected.
cargo build constraints (never two builds in one worktree) forced sequential test and gate runs.
open_items: Run `git fetch origin main && codex review --base origin/main` and fix actionable findings within the boundary, re-gating each round.
Run the review checklist against the full diff and report the final sha, each failing-first test with its oracle, codex rounds, and gate exit codes to the lead.
Run just fuzz-check and just bench only if the model public signatures change or git processes are involved; this was not determined in the transcript.
Do not push, resolve findings or open PRs; wait for the lead's go-ahead.
